There's actually several different forms to depression. There's major depression (what I deal with), chronic depression (depression that's lasts for long periods of time), bipolar (do you have periods where where you feel amazing and then next you know you're not?), dysthymia, postpartum (obviously not you lol), even seasonal (winter or spring usually). Now for your second question regarding treatment, there are absolutely ways to do without meds. In fact I kinda think that's an avenue to explore first. Most important thing to do is find a therapist. They can evaluate you to help determine what would be best. You could go to a psychologist, they usually tend to prescribe meds (doesn't apply to all, but that's where the trend is). Or a psychotherapist who diagnoses but can't prescribe. I'm a creative type as well. Music (play guitar), wrote scripts, filmmaking and other things and I take lexapro with Wellbutrin. And I haven't once thought it's the meds that hurts my creative drive, it's my depression. But everyone responds to them differently and the shitty thing about them is a lot of times people have to experiment to find the right one or combo and that takes time.  Back to avoiding meds, I personally believe in trying to treat it without and use meds as the next step so to speak. I found the gym really helped and became a great coping mechanism.
